main.label: good
main.text: The first thing push does is check top == CAPACITY - 1. top is the index of the last stored item, so when it equals CAPACITY - 1 the array is full, and writing to data[top + 1] would go past the end of the array. In that case push returns false, so the caller sees that the value was not stored, and neither data nor top changes.

followUp.label: good
followUp.text: The check guards the array bounds. With CAPACITY 4 the valid indexes are 0 to 3, so once top is 3 another write would hit data[4], which is out of bounds. Returning false is how the caller learns that the push failed.

main.label: good
main.text: The loop calls push with 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60. The first four succeed because top goes from -1 up to 3. The fifth and sixth find top equal to 3, so push returns false, and main prints 'Full at 5' and 'Full at 6'.

followUp.label: good
followUp.text: So only 10 to 40 are stored. The values 50 and 60 are dropped, because a failed push does not change the stack.

main.label: good
main.text: top is the index of the most recent element. pop first copies data[top] into out and only then does top--. If it decremented first it would read the slot below the top, and the real top value would be lost. The old slot is just left as stale data that the next push overwrites.

followUp.label: good
followUp.text: It is about order: read data[top] while top still points at the last item, then move top down by one. After the decrement the element is logically gone, even though the old value is still sitting in the array.

main.label: good
main.text: The while loop calls pop until it returns false. The stack holds 10 20 30 40 with 40 on top, so it prints 40 30 20 10, last in first out. Then pop finds top == -1 and returns false, which ends the loop.

followUp.label: good
followUp.text: Last in, first out: 40 was pushed last so it comes out first. The loop stops cleanly because pop returns false once top is below zero.

main.text: size returns top + 1. After the four pops top is back to -1, so size() returns 0 and main prints 'Size: 0'. top + 1 works because top is an index and the number of items is one more than the last index.

followUp.label: good
followUp.text: Since top starts at -1 for an empty stack, top + 1 is 0 when empty and 4 when full, so it always equals the number of stored items.
